name: Intellia Therapeutics
upcoming_dates: 2027-03-10 | regulatory | FDA PDUFA target action date for the lonvo-z BLA in hereditary angioedema | https://ir.intelliatx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/intellia-therapeutics-announces-fda-acceptance-biologics-license | primary
product: Lonvo-z (lonvoguran ziclumeran), a one-time in vivo CRISPR therapy inactivating KLKB1 to permanently lower kallikrein, for hereditary angioedema; Phase 3 HAELO cut mean monthly attacks 87% vs placebo and left 62% attack-free and therapy-free for six months (2026-08-06, ir.intelliatx.com). Nex-z targets ATTR amyloidosis.
demand: Not applicable yet: pre-commercial with no product revenue. Q2 2026 collaboration revenue fell to $7.7M from $14.2M a year earlier (2026-08-06, ir.intelliatx.com). Growth today is milestone and financing driven, not price, volume or mix.
pricing_power: Pre-revenue, so no margins yet. Risks: high cost of goods for one-time LNP and CRISPR manufacturing; commercial buildout lifted Q2 2026 G&A to $37.8M from $27.2M (2026-08-06); weak payer pricing or a restrictive HLA or liver-monitoring label would compress future margins.
competition: No Chinese low-cost in vivo CRISPR HAE substitute found. Closest cheaper alternatives are daily oral small-molecule prophylaxis and on-demand C1-inhibitor, neither replicating one-time durability (2026-09-08, ir.intelliatx.com). Not found for a Chinese equivalent.
market_strategy: CEO John Leonard, 2026-09-08: our team is well prepared to deliver this one-time treatment to patients who are waiting for new options. On 2026-08-06 he said Intellia expects FDA BLA acceptance in H2 2026, a U.S. launch in H1 2027, and MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment completion in H2 2026 (ir.intelliatx.com).
bull: FDA accepted lonvo-z BLA with Priority Review on 2026-09-08, PDUFA 2027-03-10, no adcom planned; Phase 3 HAELO cut attacks 87%, 62% attack-free; $400M non-dilutive OrbiMed loan plus $628.4M cash into 2028 funds launch.
bear: Pre-revenue: Q2 2026 collaboration revenue fell to $7.7M from $14.2M; G&A rose to $37.8M from $27.2M; nex-z liver-enzyme elevations clustered in one HLA allele raise label or monitoring risk; payer reimbursement for one-time high-cost therapy unproven.
falsifier: An FDA complete response letter for the lonvo-z BLA on or before the 2027-03-10 PDUFA date, or a label requiring HLA or liver monitoring or a boxed warning.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 30d: 2026-09-08 FDA accepted the lonvo-z BLA for HAE with Priority Review, PDUFA 2027-03-10; 2026-09-04 a $400M non-dilutive OrbiMed loan, $75M upfront (ir.intelliatx.com). Last 90d: Q2 results 2026-08-06 (cash $628.4M into 2028); additional HAELO Phase 3 data and NEJM paper 2026-06-13.
web_true_now_not_modelled: On 2026-09-08 FDA advised it is not currently planning an advisory committee for lonvo-z, removing an adcom binary and fixing 2027-03-10 (ir.intelliatx.com). The 2026-08-06 release disclosed the highest nex-z liver-enzyme elevations occurred in one HLA allele, a monitoring or label risk analysts may not have modelled.
web_demand_product: Lonvo-z (lonvoguran ziclumeran), a one-time in vivo CRISPR therapy inactivating KLKB1 to permanently lower kallikrein, for hereditary angioedema; Phase 3 HAELO cut mean monthly attacks 87% vs placebo and left 62% attack-free and therapy-free for six months (2026-08-06, ir.intelliatx.com). Nex-z targets ATTR amyloidosis.
web_price_volume_mix: Not applicable yet: pre-commercial with no product revenue. Q2 2026 collaboration revenue fell to $7.7M from $14.2M a year earlier (2026-08-06, ir.intelliatx.com). Growth today is milestone and financing driven, not price, volume or mix.
web_bottleneck: The company bottleneck is payer reimbursement and launch execution for a one-time high-cost therapy, plus LNP and CRISPR manufacturing scale. It relieves the patient bottleneck of lifelong chronic prophylaxis needing IV or SC as often as twice weekly or daily oral dosing (2026-09-08, ir.intelliatx.com).
web_who_benefits_next: Regeneron (25% ATTR cost and profit share, nex-z partner), LNP and CDMO manufacturers, HAE treatment centres and HLA and genetic-testing labs, milestone lender OrbiMed, and the wider in vivo gene-editing field a first approval would validate (2026-08-06 and 2026-09-04, ir.intelliatx.com).
web_who_loses: Makers of chronic HAE prophylaxis if a one-time therapy wins: Takeda with Takhzyro, BioCryst with Orladeyo, CSL Behring, plus oral rivals Pharvaris and KalVista; in ATTR, Alnylam, BridgeBio and Pfizer. Basis: it displaces the chronic lifelong dosing described 2026-09-08 at ir.intelliatx.com.
web_margin_collapse_risk: Pre-revenue, so no margins yet. Risks: high cost of goods for one-time LNP and CRISPR manufacturing; commercial buildout lifted Q2 2026 G&A to $37.8M from $27.2M (2026-08-06); weak payer pricing or a restrictive HLA or liver-monitoring label would compress future margins.
web_low_cost_substitute: No Chinese low-cost in vivo CRISPR HAE substitute found. Closest cheaper alternatives are daily oral small-molecule prophylaxis and on-demand C1-inhibitor, neither replicating one-time durability (2026-09-08, ir.intelliatx.com). Not found for a Chinese equivalent.
web_ceo_promised: CEO John Leonard, 2026-09-08: our team is well prepared to deliver this one-time treatment to patients who are waiting for new options. On 2026-08-06 he said Intellia expects FDA BLA acceptance in H2 2026, a U.S. launch in H1 2027, and MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment completion in H2 2026 (ir.intelliatx.com).
web_did_they_deliver: Yes on the near-term promise: Intellia guided FDA BLA acceptance for H2 2026 (2026-08-06) and FDA accepted it with Priority Review on 2026-09-08. It also delivered the promised EAACI presentation and NEJM publication on 2026-06-13. Launch and MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment stay open.
web_what_would_falsify: An FDA complete response letter for the lonvo-z BLA on or before the 2027-03-10 PDUFA date, or a label requiring HLA or liver monitoring or a boxed warning; a U.S. launch slipping past H1 2027; or a dilutive equity raise replacing the milestone-based debt (2026-09-04).
